purpose: First real-weights check of Stellan-Run's image encoder (the eye) against llama.cpp's clip encoder

hardware.cpu: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz (4 vCPU cloud VM)

encoder.note: Uploaded 2025-05-01 with clip.use_gelu=true from Mistral's original config; Mistral corrected hidden_act to silu on 2025-05-09 (commit 73ce7c62b9). Stellan-Run always runs SiLU and reports file_says_gelu. For a like-for-like comparison llama.cpp ran a copy with the key renamed to clip.use_silu.

optimisation_steps_same_image.step: int8 Q8_0 kernel with 256-value activation blocks
AVX2 attention with per-head contiguous keys and values
32-value activation blocks (as llama.cpp), cache-blocked rows x tokens

limitations: One synthetic image, one machine, three rounds: directional.
Stellan-Run's projector uses exact GELU; llama.cpp uses the tanh approximation, which explains part of the remaining difference.
Neither Lite nor Max can use these embeddings yet: the projectors must be trained (see HANDOVER.md).
PNG/JPEG decoding is not in Stellan-Run; `see` takes raw RGB.
